newsitem.title: FRANCE: Court to rule on powers in Chronopost/express case.
newsitem.headline: Court to rule on powers in Chronopost/express case.

text.p: The Paris Commercial Ccourt is due to rule on January 28 on whether it is competent to judge a long-running case opposing French-based express distributors and Chronopost, the express arm of the French post office, officials from both parties involved told Reuters.

The case, which has also been before the European Commission and the European Court of Justice, centres on claims by the Syndicat Francais de l'Express International (SFEI) that the French post office provided aid to Chronopost during 1986-1991 in contravention of EU competition rules.

"The aid to Chronopost took the form of logistical support from the postal utility's personnel, vehicles and post offices, sales and marketing force - for which the real market price' was 850 million francs," an SFEI official told Reuters
"In addition, the private express operators' market share was affected by this aid representing a financial prejudice of some 216 million francs," he said.
The official added: "We think the commercial court is the right forum for this case to be heard as it concerns commercial activities."
In a statement, Chronopost said the case should be heard by an administrative court as the post office was under state administration until 1990.
The EU's Court of First Instance recently rejected SFEI's claims that the French post office had abused its dominant position in aiding Chronopost.
